Author: T. Vinod Kumar
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 Writ Petition No.24660 of 2023
Order:

This Writ Petition is filed to declare the action of respondent No.2 in interfering with the possession of the petitioner in building and property admeasuring 195 sq. yards bearing H.No.10-36,
Peerzadiguda, Uppal, Hyderabad and threatening to demolish part of the building under the guise of widening of the existing road to 100 feet leading from Peerzadiguda Kaman to Pratapsingaram without following due process of law by initiating land acquisition proceedings or paying compensation to the petitioner and also compelling the petitioner to accept the Transferable Development Rights (TDR) being offered by petitioner as illegal, arbitrary, unconstitutional and also in violation of Article 14 and 300-A of the Constitution of India apart from being contrary to the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act').
2.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for petitioner, learned Government Pleader for Municipal Administration and Urban Development appearing for respondent No.1 and Sri B.Jagan Madhav Rao, learned Standing Counsel appearing for respondent No.2, and perused the record.
With their consent, the Writ Petition is taken up for hearing at admission stage.

3. Petitioner contends that he is the owner and possessor of house bearing No.10-36 admeasuring 195 sq. yds situated at Peerjadiguda, Uppal, Hyderabad; that a part of the said house is sought to be demolished by respondents under the guise of the same being required for 100 ft road widening;
that petitioner has been offered TDR in respect of the property being affected by demolition in the road widening; that the petitioner is not aggreable for accepting the TDR being offered by respondent No.2; and that the respondents cannot compel the petitioner to accept the TDR in lieu of the respondent authorities following due process of law for acquisition of petitioner's subject property.

4. Learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.2 has placed before this Court the written instructions dated 12-09-2023 under the signature of the Commissioner, Municipal Corporation, Peerzadiguda.

The same are taken on record.
5.

By the said written instructions, it is stated that there is a plan to extend the existing 40 feet road from Peerzadiguda Kaman to Pratapsingaram to 100 feet road gradually to cater to the growing Dayanand Ghanathe vs The State Of Telangana on 12 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34313097/
1 traffic needs; and that petitioner's house gets affected if the road extension is undertaken.

sentences.text:
However,
it is stated that no steps with regard to petitioner's property are initiated by respondent No.2.
6.

By the said written instructions, it is also stated that almost all the house and plot owners of the road affected area on Peerzadiguda Kaman to Pratapsingaram road have voluntarily agreed to receive compensation in the form of TDR and surrendered the road affected area of their property in public interest.

By the said written instructions, it is also sated that respondent No.2, in accordance with the Government Policy, is ready to offer compensation to the petitioner herein in the form of TDR at the rate of 400% of the road affected area if petitioner surrenders part of his property for the purpose of road widening.
7. I have noted respective contentions urged.
8. Admittedly, petitioner is not in agreement to accept the TDR being offered by respondents.
No person can be deprived or compelled to part with his property under Article 300-A of the Constitution of India without following due process of law.

Since the petitioner is not willing to accept the TDR being offered by respondent authorities, the only recourse available to the respondents is to acquire the land of petitioner by following due process of law by initiating proceedings under as contemplated under the Act.

9. In Channavajala Vijaya Lakshmi Vs. State of Telangana 1 this Court held that it is incumbent on the part of the State to initiate proceedings under Section 32 of the Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority Act, 2008 in accordance with the provisions of the Act for acquisition of the portion of the land required by them for road widening out of the property owned by the petitioner and pay compensation to the petitioner.

entities.text: Channavajala Vijaya Lakshmi Vs. State of Telangana 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If not, the petitioner would be deprived of his valuable property without compensation 10.

In view of settled legal position as stated supra, and in the facts and circumstances of the case, if the respondent authorities 2015(5) ALT 620 require the land of petitioner for the purpose of road widening, they shall initiate proceedings as contemplated under the Act.
11. Subject to the above observations and directions, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
12. It is made clear that this Court has not expressed any view on the merits of the claims of the contesting parties.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending if any shall stand closed.
No costs.
